This Miscellaneous First Appeal is filed under Section 54(1) of L.A.Act, praying to set aside the judgment and award dated 22.03.2010 passed by the Civil Judge (Sr.Dn.) at Basavakalyan in No.45/2007 and pleased to modify by allowing the appeal by enhancing the compensation at Rs.6,00,000/- per acre to the Wet land from Rs.3,00,000/-
per acre to the wet land of the appellants with all statutory benefits and with cost.

These appeals having been heard through physical hearing / video conference and reserved for Judgment on 20.01.2023, coming on for pronouncement of Judgment this day, T.G.Shivashankare Gowda, J., delivered the following:
 MFA.200436/2014  C/w MFA.200410/2014  MFA.200437/2014  5 Pandurang S/O Husanappa And Ors vs The Spl.Land Acquisition Officer on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24378814/
3  JUDGMENT

The appellants in these appeals have challenged the judgment and award dated 22.03.2010 passed in L.A.C.No.58/2007, 38/2008 and 45/2007 respectively, on the file of the Civil Judge (Sr.Dn.) at Basavakalyan, (hereinafter referred to as 'Reference Court' for short), seeking enhancement of compensation in respect of the acquired wet lands situated at Kalkhora village of Basavakalyan Taluk, Bidar District.
2. The appellants were the claimants and the respondent was the Special Land Acquisition Officer ('SLAO' for brevity) before the reference court.
For the purpose of convenience, the parties will be referred to as per their status before the trial court.
3. Facts in brief are, for the construction of New Okaly Tank, an extent of 100 acres of land was acquired by the Government of Karnataka vide preliminary notification dated 12.05.2005.
An award was passed fixing the market value of wet and dry lands Rs.30,429/- and Rs.24,343/- per acre.
The claimants protested the award which resulted in a reference to the civil court for determination of correct market value.
The reference court awarded Rs.3,00,000/- and Rs.1,60,000/- per acre for wet and dry lands respectively.
4. Seeking enhancement, the claimants are before this court on the grounds that the compensation is inadequate; and the method adopted in arriving at compensation is not proper.
They have sought re- assessment, and enhancement from Rs.3,00,000/- to Rs.6,00,000/- per acre for wet lands.
5. We have heard the arguments of Sri.A.M.Biradar, learned counsel for the claimants and Sri.Mallikarjun C.Basareddy, learned Government Advocate for the SLAO.

6. It is the contention of the learned counsel for the claimants that the reference court has adopted the capitalization method in assessing the compensation inspite of the claimants demonstrating that relating to acquisition of similar lands for the same purpose, the reference court in L.A.C.No.111/2019, awarded compensation of Rs.9,25,752/- for the wet land.
Since the difference in notification was just two years, applying de-escalation at the rate of 3% the appellants have sought to fix the compensation accordingly.
7. To support his contention, he has relied upon the judgment of this court in Gundappa -vs- State of Karnataka1.
This court while dealing with a case of enhancement of similar lands acquired after long gap of 15 years, held that parties were entitled to appreciation at the rate of 3% per annum.
Per contra, learned Government Advocate has contended that the acquired lands were notified on 12.05.2005 whereas the lands in LAC No.111/19 were notified on 05.04.2007.
There is a gap of two years; subsequent notification cannot be a guiding factor for determining the compensation.

He has further contended that the method adopted by the reference court is correct, there is no need for Pandurang S/O Husanappa And Ors vs The Spl.Land Acquisition Officer on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24378814/
4 enhancement of compensation and supported the impugned judgment.
9.

sentences.text: We have given our anxious consideration to the arguments addressed before us and perused the materials on record.
10. The reference court has adopted the method of capitalization as it is more suited to determine the market value of the acquired lands.
The reference court has assessed the income from jowar and toor crops being grown in the dry land.
The reference Court assessed yield of 8 quintals of jowar, 4 carts load of jowar fodder, 8 qunitals of toor per acre.

The reference court has considered Rs.1,300/-
per quintal for jowar, Rs.250/- per cart load for jowar fodder, Rs.2,385/- per quintal for toor as price prevailing at the time of acquisition. The value of jowar (Rs.1,300/- x 6=Rs.7,800/-), jowar fodder (Rs.250/- x 4=Rs.1,000/-) and toor (Rs.2,385/- x 8=Rs.19,080/-), in all Rs.27,880/-, and after deducting 40% cultivation cost i.e., Rs.11,152/- and arrived at Rs.16,728/-.
By applying the multiplier of '10', the market value was assessed at Rs.1,67,280/- and accordingly rounded of to Rs.1,60,000/- as the market value per acre of dry land.
11. Insofar as the wet land is concerned, the reference court has observed that the claimants were growing sugar cane, bananas, onions, vegetables, etc.,.
For the purpose of capitalization, the crop is taken as Banana.
In one acre of land 1200 banana plants can be planted each bunch of banana is valued at Rs.50/-.
Therefore from 1200 plants, expected income was Rs.60,000/- and deducting 50% towards cultivation cost, the market value can be computed at Rs.3,00,000/- per acre of wet land.
12. It is pertinent to note that the Deputy Director of Horticulture, Gulbarga, under Ex.P46 certified that per acre of wet land, 1210 banana plants can be planted.

The APMC, Gulbarga, certifies under Ex.P45/certificate that per bunch of banana weighs between 10 and 20 kgs., and categorized the price of banana in three different qualities, viz., low quality - Rs.350/- per quintal, medium quality - Rs.430/- per quintal and high quality - Rs.480/- per quintal.
If these aspects are taken into consideration, in 1 acre of land, 1210 bunches of banana can be grown weighing average of 15 kgs.
per bunch with average price of Rs.420/- per quintal, then the price of 1 acre of land can be calculated at 1210x15 = 18150 kgs./100 = 181.5 quintals x Rs.420/- = Rs.76,230/-.
If 50% of the cultivation cost is excluded, it comes to Rs.38,115/- with '10' multiplier comes to Rs.3,81,150/-.
Keeping this in mind, let us proceed further.
13. Since in wet lands, sugarcane is also grown with onion and other vegetables, going with single crop is not proper.

That apart, in the very same village, lands were acquired for the same purpose just two years after the present acquisition and compensation was awarded in LAC No.111/2019 and therefore, placing reliance on the said judgment is not bad, as we have an instance of determination of market value of the same lands is available on hand in order to achieve uniformity.
14.
Copy of the judgment has not been placed before the reference court for consideration.
On its perusal, it is pertinent to note that the lands pertain to the same village were acquired for the identical purpose under preliminary notification dated 05.04.2007.

In this judgment, the very reference Court has fixed the market value at Rs.6,17,168/- for the dry lands and Rs.9,25,752/- for Pandurang S/O Husanappa And Ors vs The Spl.Land Acquisition Officer on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24378814/

sentences.text: the wet lands.
Within a span of two years, there is a huge difference in market price and this can be noticed, because of Okaly Tank project, the land at Kolkhora village has taken the surge increase in the price.
Hence, this court has to consider what could be escalation and de-escalation of market prices.

15. Adverting to the argument of the learned counsel for the claimants with reference to escalation at 3%, it is seen that in LAC No.111/2019, the reference court has considered the compensation awarded to lands acquired to Lower Mullamari project, compensation was determined at Rs.3,75,322/- for dry lands in the year 1999.
The reference court allowed escalation of 8% per annum in coming to the conclusion of Rs.6,17,168/- per acre of the land in the year 2007.
If the compensation was determined in LAC No.111/2019 allowing escalation of 8% of appreciation, the argument of the learned counsel for the claimants for de-escalation of 3% has no logic.
16. In Gundappa's case (supra) while allowing 3% of appreciation, there was a long gap of 15 years in determining the compensation.
In Gundappa's case (supra), this court has relied on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Ranjit Singh and others -vs- Union Territory of Chandigarh2.

entities.text: Ranjit Singh and others -vs- Union Territory of Chandigarh2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court at para-6 of the judgment while considering the land acquired pursuant to the preliminary notification published on 03.12.1975 held that, the market value fixed for similar lands acquired under a previous notification published on 23.12.1974, the market value AIR 1977 SC 227 has been enhanced from Rs.33,000/- per acre to Rs.36,000/- per acre by adopting escalation of 9%.

Therefore, we find no force in the argument of the learned counsel for the claimants that de-escalation shall be 3% when the very reliance placed speaks of escalation of 9% for one year.
17.

In view of these factors, for a period of eight years, the escalation was given at 8%, for a gap of 15 years, the escalation was given at 3% and for a gap of one year, the Hon'ble Apex Court has given escalation of 9%.

In the facts and circumstances of this case, we are of the considered opinion that de-escalation has to be considered not less than 10% as the surge in the price was on account of establishment of Okaly Tank Project.
Hence, the de-escalation has to be calculated accordingly.
18. If the lands in the year 2007 cost Rs.6,17,168/- for the dry lands, the reference court calculated as 1.5 times will be the price of wet lands.
The same could be followed here in this case also for calculating the market value by applying 10% de- escalation for two years.
The market value of wet lands determined in LAC No.111/2019 is Rs.9,25,752/- per acre and de-escalation of 10% is applied for one year, then deduction comes to Rs.1,85,150/- for 2 years.
If it is deducted, then the market value of the wet land stands at Rs.7,40,601/- rounded off to Rs.7,40,000/- per acre.

19. The evidence on record though determines the market value on the basis of the capitalization method, it may not depict correct market value of the acquired lands based on single crop when multiple crops were being grown.
The correct market value has been determined by the Reference court to the very same village was enhanced by this court.

In view of the principles of law enunciated for escalation and de- escalation, it is proper to apply de-escalation of market value determined for Kalkhora village in the year 2007 to determine the market value for the year 2005.
Hence, the compensation so assessed by the reference court at Rs.3,00,000/- per acre of wet land does not depict the correct market value.

We assess Rs.7,40,000/- as the correct market value per acre of Pandurang S/O Husanappa And Ors vs The Spl.Land Acquisition Officer on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24378814/
6 acquired wet land and accordingly, the appeals deserve to be allowed.

20. In the result, we pass the following;
 ORDER  (i) All the appeals are allowed.
(ii) The impugned judgment and award is  hereby modified.
(iii) The market value of the acquired wet land is fixed at Rs.7,40,000/- per acre instead of Rs.3,00,000/- fixed by the Reference court with other statutory benefits.
(iv) Rest of the judgment of the reference court stands unaltered.
